Pilot programs have been implemented for customers who want to do dimming and capture energy savings, with rebate/refund checks issued based on the verified energy savings. Rebate programs have also existed for LED conversion in some cases. 13. Do you believe that there would have been adoption without the electric utility’s support? The respondents had mixed opinions on whether adaptive lighting technology adoption would have been possible without the support of electric utilities. The co-ops and municipalities were more open to adopting it, while IOUs were resistant. The rebate program offered by the utility was important for the financial viability of the project. The utility’s support and partnership were necessary, especially if they owned the streetlights. The utility needs to do calculations to determine the load on the electrical infrastructure and ensure that the city is not getting free energy. For flat rate billing, there may not be an incentive for the utility to implement dimming systems unless the city can show additional environmental benefits. 14. Is your engagement with the electric utility still ongoing? If yes, what form does this take? Responses to the question, “Is your engagement with the electric utility still ongoing? If yes, what form does this take?” varied. One stakeholder mentioned that once rebates were complete, there was no ongoing engagement beyond regular charges. Another stakeholder suspected that engagement had likely ended. Stakeholder 3 mentioned that they might engage with clients after construction for evaluations or other projects, and finally another stakeholder mentioned ongoing challenges with data and metering issues with the utility. 15. Is there a “How to Why to” guide for adopting adaptive lighting technology? In response to the question about a “How to Why to” guide for adopting adaptive lighting technology, the participants had varied responses. One stakeholder suggested that the best guide was the one created for the City of Denver and Colorado Department of Transportation, while another said there was nothing. Another stakeholder mentioned that the International Dark-Sky Association might have something, and also mentioned the annex in RP8 and some lighting guidelines from cities in Canada. One stakeholder was not aware of any such guide but felt that a standard practice guide would always be helpful. 16. Will this “How to Why to” guide be of any relevance to you? Or do you think that your adoption process can now be considered complete? The responses were mixed. One person believed that the guide would provide credibility to their adoption process, while others think that it would be helpful to have a guide to learn from and avoid potential issues. Another stakeholder believed that the time is right for such a guide, as there are enough installed projects to learn from.
